primitives.name: Perception as Belief
primitives.verbatim_quote: Any object which remains uncontradicted is ipso facto believed and posited as absolute reality.
primitives.assumptions: The assumption is that perception directly equates to belief without requiring additional validation or contradiction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When contradictory evidence emerges, the perceived reality collapses into uncertainty.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, this maps to conformal prediction intervals where uncontradicted outcomes become the posterior belief state. In GSE, it corresponds to a state-transition kernel that updates beliefs based on consistent observations.
layer2.telemetry: Measurable shifts in predictive confidence when new data either supports or contradicts existing perceptual models.

primitives.name: Object Existence Incompatibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: If either of them say, That candle or that horse, even when I don't see it, exists in the outer world,' he pushes intothe outer world'an object which may be incompatible with everything which he otherwise knows of that world.
primitives.assumptions: The assumption is that introducing an object into a known system requires consistency with all prior knowledge of that system.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inconsistency between the introduced object and established knowledge creates a singularity, leading to model rejection.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, this maps to Bayesian model selection where hypotheses incompatible with prior data are automatically penalized. In GSE, it corresponds to a situational reasoning kernel that flags actions violating environmental constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Detection of empirical anomalies that violate previously established behavioral or physical laws.

primitives.name: Mental Object Situation
primitives.verbatim_quote: But they are situated in their own spaces, the space in which they severally appear, and neither of those spaces is the space in which the realities calledthe outer world'exist.
primitives.assumptions: The assumption is that mental constructs occupy distinct representational spaces separate from physical reality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When mental models attempt to map onto incompatible external spaces, the representation fails.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, this maps to state-space duality where latent variables (mental objects) operate in a different metric than observed variables (outer world). In GSE, it corresponds to a derived kernel that maintains separate state manifolds for perception and action.
layer2.telemetry: Quantifying the discrepancy between internal state representations and external environmental coordinates.

primitives.name: Dream Horse Wings
primitives.verbatim_quote: If I merely dream of a horse with wings, my horse interferes with nothing else and has not to be contradicted.
primitives.assumptions: The assumption is that internally generated narratives lack the external referents necessary for contradiction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Self-consistent internal stories remain coherent but fail to interface with empirical reality.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, this maps to self-consistent generative models that produce coherent samples but do not align with out-of-distribution test sets. In GSE, it corresponds to a derived kernel for planning loops that operate within simulated rather than physical state spaces.
layer2.telemetry: Measuring the divergence between internally simulated trajectories and externally observed outcomes.

The core insight is that belief formation operates as a unification process: an idea becomes reality only when it resists contradiction across multiple frames of reference. This mirrors modern statistical learning theory where a hypothesis gains credibility through repeated non-rejection under diverse testing conditions. The 'incompatibility' described is mathematically equivalent to a likelihood ratio test comparing the introduced object against background knowledge; if the likelihood is zero, the object is rejected. Mental objects occupying separate topological spaces suggest a bundle structure in differential geometry, where the brain's internal manifold is a fiber over the external sensory base. Dream logic exemplifies a closed system with no boundary conditions, analogous to autonomous dynamical systems that evolve without environmental coupling.
